name: gmail-filters
description: Propose Gmail filters from triage evidence (JSONL, one record per message) — a sender is proposed only when every observed message was zero-touch — and export the operator-approved rows as a Gmail-importable mailFilters.xml; one-click (RFC 8058) unsubscribe from an operator-signed approval list behind --yes; no Gmail writes, no credential
surface: local-only CLI; no Gmail API client, no OAuth, no write scope; `plan` writes a 600-mode plan file, `export` writes approved rows only as mailFilters.xml the operator imports by hand; one non-zero-touch message blocks a sender; trash needs a policy match plus a second approval; never overwrites, never writes into `/`, `$HOME` or the belt; `--live` counts via read-only `gmh list`; `unsub-plan` classifies unsubscribe methods from export headers; `unsubscribe` sends RFC 8058 one-click POSTs only for an operator-signed approval list, previewing until the operator's `--yes`; audit log

origin.note: authored in this belt; composes with tools/gmail-harvest (read-only) for --live counts

install.description: Put gmf on PATH by linking the brew bin dir at the belt's copy
install.why: the review loop (plan → show → export) is typed by hand from wherever the evidence and plan live
install.yes: /opt/homebrew/bin/gmf points at tools/gmail-filters/gmf.mjs; `gmf` works from any directory
install.no: nothing changes; call it as `node {TOOLBELT}/tools/gmail-filters/gmf.mjs` or `toolbelt run gmf -- …`

env.name: GMF_POLICY
env.description: Path to the sender policy (default ~/.config/toolbelt/gmail-filters/policy.json, mode 600)

env.name: GMH_BIN
env.description: gmh executable `plan --live` calls (default {TOOLBELT}/tools/gmail-harvest/gmh.mjs, run under node)

auth.flow: gmf holds no credential. `plan --live` runs `gmh list`, which reads Gmail on gmh's own gmail.readonly grant (tools/gmail-harvest); without --live gmf touches no network

safeguards: No Gmail write code exists: no API client, no OAuth, no scope; the only network path is `plan --live`, which runs the read-only `gmh list` via execFile (SENSIBILITIES #1)

The never-filter-important-mail rule is code: a sender is proposed only when every observed message is in cleanup or auto_handled; one message in any other bucket (or none) blocks it and lists it under `blocked`; a message seen in several runs keeps every bucket it was given; a domain filter needs ≥2 addresses that each qualify and no blocked or protected address at that domain

Trash is never proposed unless the sender matches the policy trash list, and then the row carries requires_explicit_approval; export emits shouldTrash only when the row has both approved: true and approved_trash: true, and refuses a trash action without them
Export renders only rows whose approved is the JSON boolean true, refuses a row whose criteria differ from the query its match builds (what was reviewed is what exports), and XML-escapes every value
Ceilings are code constants in gmf.mjs: MAX_FILTERS 200 per plan, MIN_EVIDENCE 3 by default with a floor of 2 (a lower --min is refused) (SENSIBILITIES #3)
Output is contained: plan and XML files are created 600 and never overwrite; `/`, $HOME itself and any path inside the Toolbelt tree are refused, because both files name senders

One audit line per verb run to stderr and ~/.local/share/toolbelt/gmail-filters/audit.log (dir 700, file 600): timestamp, verb, input and output paths, counts — never a sender or message content (SENSIBILITIES #7)

The operator's sender policy lives outside the tree at ~/.config/toolbelt/gmail-filters/policy.json and a group/world-readable one is refused; the tree carries only policy.json.example (SENSIBILITIES #11)

verbs.name: plan
verbs.note: reads evidence JSONL, writes a 600-mode plan file the operator named (or stdout); --live adds gmh list counts (gmail.readonly)

verbs.name: show
verbs.note: the plan as a table; reads a local file

verbs.name: export
verbs.note: approved rows → a new 600-mode mailFilters.xml the operator named; never overwrites; --explain writes nothing. Import into Gmail is the human's step in the web UI

verbs.name: create / delete Gmail filters (settings.filters.*)
verbs.note: no Gmail API code and no gmail.settings.basic scope in this phase

verbs.name: modify labels / archive / mark read (messages.modify, batchModify, labels.*)
verbs.note: no modify code and no gmail.modify scope; existing mail is untouched

verbs.name: trash / delete messages
verbs.note: no trash or delete code; shouldTrash exists only as an XML property the human imports

verbs.name: unsub-plan
verbs.note: headers of gmh export directories → candidates file (method one_click/mailto/landing/none, target host, DKIM alignment); no network; writes a new 600-mode file the operator named, never overwrites

verbs.name: unsubscribe
verbs.note: RFC 8058 one-click POST to each sender on an operator-signed approval file (schema gmail-filters.unsubscribe/1: approved_by + the operator's words); previews and sends nothing without --yes; https public hosts only, no cookies or credentials, redirects followed only with --follow-redirects; at most MAX_UNSUB 100 per run; resumable results log (600) beside the approval; read back later with gmh list

verbs.name: unsubscribe by mailto / landing page
verbs.note: no code sends mail or drives a browser; senders without one-click get a filter instead

risk.worst_case: an approved unsubscribe cannot be undone by gmf (resubscribe by hand at the sender); writes a plan and an XML file naming the operator's senders to a local path the operator chose; a filter only reaches Gmail when the operator imports the XML by hand, and a wrongly approved filter archives (or, with double approval, trashes) matching new mail until deleted

checks.label: gmf sender policy (~/.config/toolbelt/gmail-filters/policy.json): mode 600, valid labels and lists
gmh present for `plan --live` (optional)
checks.fix: plan --live needs tools/gmail-harvest; without it plan runs evidence-only

smoke_test.expect: usage renders; unit and CLI tests green — no network, no Gmail

do_not_vendor: any plan.json or mailFilters.xml (sender addresses; containment refuses the tree)
